result:
I played all 24 months. Net cost was **$1,236.7M**, with no penalties: all three training runs were met and all inference demand was served every month.

**Settlement ($M):**
| | |
|---|---|
| Spent | 1,432.1 (GPUs 1,000; power 252; cloud contracts 285; resale −104.8; spot 0; unserved 0) |
| Contracts still owed after month 23 | +95.5 |
| GPUs left, valued at month 24 | −291.0 |
| **Net cost** | **1,236.7** |

**How it went:**
- **Months 0 and 4:** I ordered 40k gen H GPUs and signed 80 MW of extra power (50 MW + 30 MW) so the new GPUs could run. I also reserved 8 kH of cloud capacity for 24 months at $1.44M per kH-month.
- **Months 5–15:** Export controls and tight supply slowed deliveries to under 1k a month for a while. The queue had been ordered early, so it still finished shipping by month 17.
- **Gen N launched in month 18, as the rumours suggested.** I sold 3k gen H GPUs the month before, while they still held their full price. In months 21–23 I sold 9k more spare GPUs. In all, resales brought in $104.8M.
- **I never used spot or reserved anything extra.** That kept costs down, but it means I was relying on the GPU queue alone for the final window.

**Main inefficiency:** I bought more than I needed. Training finished with large surpluses: 182 against 60 needed in the first window and 316 against 140 in the second. That spare capacity was wasted, because compute only counts in the window it falls in. Power is the other cost: both new power contracts run 24 months from their start dates, past month 23, which accounts for about $84M of the $95.5M owed at settlement. Ordering about 10k fewer GPUs, or signing less power, would probably have lowered the total.
